reviews.text: I'm honestly digging it so far, one of those easy to learn difficult to master games. Good music, good pixel art, interesting progression (though if it's possible I'd love to learn how to increase base mana/souls at the beginning of a run). Feels like I lose everything except unlocks on a new run or even a new chapter. Can't complain for the price though
Some nice concepts, but still needs further refining. E.g. Early game farming souls is monotonous.
its a really good game for people like me who cant focus on games but are really smart i beat 3 bosses my first try i really enjoyed this

almost had me, 8 min off from getting my refund, two words: Supreme Sorcerer. Have fun trying to 'beat' the game when this character exists, game relys off of mana to play, what does sorcerer do you may ask? every turn takes your mana, lets say you get 5 mana a turn(i don't remember the exact numbers but this explains how it goes), it appears he takes anywhere between 4-6 mana a turn from you, do the math, no mana no gameplay auto loss, feel like this boss wasn't playtested, (he also spams units out every turn, units cost anywhere between like 8-15 mana at this point in the game) so your sitting over here potentially net lossing mana every turn being sucked dry at 0 while a neverending horde runs you down. Other then that, games ok, don't like consumables and that seems to be nearly half of the in-game 'cards', i feel like the deckbuilding aspect is lacking and consumables shoulda been actual cards just with tweaks or somthing, who likes consumables in deckbuilding? my final thoughts; add more variety(builds are crucial to a fun deckbuilder, and this game onlly has so many), fix supreme sorcerer, and get rid of consumables, rework them into real cards in the deck for deck variety. Would be worth 5$ if it werent for Dr.Strange bending you over in act 4 with no good counterplay

正如内容上的介绍，轻量版肉鸽，内容不是很多，但是初见着实有趣。 而且基本上是一样的流程，金币消耗提升初始魔力，收集强力卡牌，然后输出，属于前期稍微策略一丢丢，后面可以直接碾压过去（这里推荐卡牌“召唤骷髅”，1灵魂消耗，召唤5个2/2并且可以直接投放在第三区域并且可以立即做出行动，配合一个诗人强化力量加1，开局5个3/3直接贴脸，大部分头目根本来不及呼叫支援就被杀掉了）。 当然这只是一种玩法而已，并且召唤骷髅在前中期才能拿到。其他流派也可各有特色，积攒力量的恶魔，无限构筑防御的蜘蛛，骑士团的荣耀...... 但正如我所说内容少导致流派也不多，但是很期待后续的更新内容。 等内容更新了我再来更新我的评论2024/09/11

The game is not exactly bad, but it needs a lot of polishing. To start a run, you need to click start run, choose the difficulty, THEN FIGURE OUT YOU'RE SUPPOSED TO CLICK LOAD SAVE, and only afterwards you can click continue(you didn't even start yet??) to start the run. There are no buttons to exit the merchants menu, you're supposed to figure out to double-click outside the menu. Also the game is quite easy and becomes a chore to finish after the first 2 runs, the only difficulty is some of the bosses which require you to change your deck a little to be able to beat them. What i like though, is the concept, art-style, music(which is quite groovy) and the atmosphere.
的确是轻量化肉鸽，没有内容的同时偏偏主线流程还很长，你一共要打5个周目，每个周目都得从零开始，而区别只有新加了几种怪物和区域，还没有必要打。后面同质化严重。 高难方面还没什么打法策略上的变化，只是在局外资源的获取上做了调整。还得刷初始，否则遇上那个蘑菇寄生boss追杀基本就等着步数耗尽慢性死亡。 欸，但是我是免费获取的，而且打法构筑还是蛮多的，所以好评。

Completely uninteresting and dull. Pretty much everything about this game is so so so so boring. The combat is literally just unit spam and nothing more. You literally just draw cards and play them without any sort of strategy or thought. There are barely any synergies between units and honestly I could go on and on. I'm sure there's someone who enjoys this sort of completely mindless and boring gameplay, but fortunately that isn't me.

Cant understand how anybody could not recommend this game for $5. Works perfectly on deck and has very cute art direction, for what it is it's really good. Yes it lacks some complexity and synergies could be fun, but with some strategy you can almost always become nigh untouchable. For the guy complaining about menus not having exit buttons, you pee with your pants all the way down. Just press escape like has been the standard for closing windows since the button was invented

Despite my recommendation I have some criticisms. 1) The game is too easy. I haven't lost a single fight since I started playing and I've already beaten the third King. The fact that your units always have initiative over the enemy makes everything very predictable and easy. The only somewhat challenging fights are the caravan miniboss (harder than anything else in the game sadly) and the first 5-10 fights in the run when you don't yet have any decent units. But once you get even a single Wizard or Berserker, it becomes very hard to lose. 2) The fights become repetitive relatively quickly. Once you have 1 or 2 good units you can use those pretty much until the end of the map. There is a lot of unit variety, but it almost doesn't matter because the game is so easy, so you never have to experiment. 3) The sound design is not good. The overworld music is somewhat cute, but the "music" during the fights, even the boss fights, is just really boring. Despite all this I am having an enjoyable time with the game and for the low price it's really quite good.

While I really enjoyed the art, animations, (and sound, to an extent), of Necroking, the enjoyment pretty much ends there. I have to recommend that people avoid this game due to deceptive advertising as well as the fact that it's not a well designed game at all. Simply put: this game is a thousand yards long and as shallow as a puddle; entire systems and gameplay loops are broken due to poor design choices. Therefore, difficulty balance is practically non-existent with selections ranging from so mind-numbingly simple a chimp could complete the game with random inputs, to so ball-breakingly difficult that one would need eidetic memory and encyclopedic knowledge of the game to even come close to beating it. On first launch, only the lowest two difficulties out of four are unlocked. As a RealGamerTM I naturally chose the highest of the two available. I subsequently beat the entire story campaign, all 5 versions of the final boss, every mini boss (multiple times), all while taking HP damage but once during my whole first run. After that, I can not imagine what the gameplay experience is on the lowest difficulty; perhaps upon selection the game just skips to the final cutscene and unlocks all achievements for you, I dunno. I do know what the experience on the hardest difficulty is however... as well as how bizarre the balancing is across all difficulties. While on easy baby mode (2/4 difficulty) you have an infinite number of troops and a near infinite number of move tokens (bones) that allow the Necroking to move one tile each across a square grid map. This world map is like 20x20 and the game tells the player where the exit is, the player doesn't need 200+ moves at one time to paint the entire map like it's a Total War game; and there's no benefit to exploration anyway when your starting deck can beat the final boss. On the highest of the four difficulties, bones are much more limited, forcing the player to make decisions about movement, as opposed to just wandering wherever. Additionally, the selected load out/army for a given fight will "crumble" out of your card inventory after battle. COOL! Now the player has to pay close attention to what is in their inventory, and to the matchup at hand. (I should probably mention at this point that difficulty 3 of 4 has limited bones for movement, but also still has unlimited troops. That means that three of the four difficulties in this game, aren't). i.e. The GAME is only playable on the highest difficulty 4, a difficulty that requires you to have already beat the final boss twice! On any other difficulty, the player has either infinite troops, or infinite movement, or both! Therefore, on any difficulty other than 4, as you practically CANNOT LOSE, there is NO GAME! THIS MEANS THAT PLAYERS MUST 'EXPERIENCE' AN 'INTERACTIVE MOVIE' TWICE, BEFORE QUITTING AND RESTARTING DIFFICULTY FOUR! Furthermore upon beginning my first difficulty 4 run, due to the exceptional ease of difficulty 2, and despite the fact that I had already seen almost all of the content the game has to offer, I still had basically no idea how to engage with these core systems because there was never a need to. I just used the most powerful units available to steamroll every fight. 20 mana for 2 skeleknights will win any fight on level 1, including bosses with next to no input from the player whatsoever. After slogging through my first run and being annoyed by the narrative, (Why try to be SuBvErSiVe about the undead being good and humanity, evil? I bought the game in part because the steam page advertises a "dark and twisted journey" to "rise and conquer" as the Necroking of the undead. I am entirely unsure as to why the overly cutesy, feel-good, story was falsely advertised), I simply had no reason to optimize my gameplay or attempt to learn any system that I should have already learned while beating the game prior. In practically every other game I can think of that has locked/optional difficulties, lower ones force the player to engage with, and therefore learn to interact with, the core gameplay systems in the same or similar ways as the highest ones. To use Metal Gear Rising; Revengeance as an example; first time players of 3rd person action games, will find challenge on easy mode, will learn to combo attacks, parry/block, stealth kill, and how to use blade time (among other core gameplay mechanics). Platinum Games veterans will be pressed to learn the same things on the hardest initially available difficulty. Both players will improve in skill and knowledge (or they will be unable to beat the game), and the easy player can move up to normal or hard, while the hard player can unlock the even more challenging Very Hard and Revengeance difficulties by playing through the campaign as usual. Both players are able to optimize their gameplay at their respective skill levels, around the same systems and abilities; and both players are therefore able to 'git gud' and advance upward in skill. Necroking affords players no such ability to learn or improve by disengaging entire systems unnecessarily to modify difficulty. Even in spite of every aforementioned problem the game has, I may have yet persevered and learned, and optimized my gameplay, until I realized that doing so would DRAMATICALLY slow the game down. On the highest difficulty, at the most optimized level of play, where the player is forced to be as conservative as possible with their resources, fights that are four to five enemy 'waves' long can take DOZENS of rounds. Fights that, on any other difficulty would be over in two rounds, now take twenty. In other words, beating Necroking at difficulty level four will require a 1000% INCREASE TO TIME INVESTMENT when compared to any other difficulty; as you summon a few of your crappiest minions, watch them chip away at the enemy, die, get resummoned, chip, die, round after round, after round, ad infinitum. THIS was the absolute mindfreak that prompted this overlong review; and what an absolutely god-awful idea it would be to implement into any game. (Could you imagine increasing difficulty in a racing game by multiplying every lap count by ten, or by making the player's car ten times slower with no other modifications to gameplay?) In short, The Necroking has no soul (har har), leaves no reasons for players to want to play more, and is clueless about its own identity. This soullessness is further evident by the blatant false advertising in on the Steam page, which I will collate in a list below: --"Establish your empire" (there is no empire establishment in this game) --"More than 30 undead types" (the vast majority of them are essentially reskins. Are skeletons, skeleton swordsman, and skeleton spearmen all different types really? Just because they have 3, 5, and 8 power respectively? There is no tactical, functional difference between the majority of units in the game and there isn't a reason to engage with any but the most powerful) --"Engage in Intense Battles...where quick reflexes are key" (I've already explained that the battles are either so easy, or so painfully drawn out, and why they will never come close to 'intense'... but quick reflexes!? This is a turn based combat system! With a pause! What are they thinking!?) --"Upgrade your units skills" (units have linear improvements that transform them into new units, nowhere are unit skills upgradeable/modifiable. In my opinion you can't claim BOTH that skills are upgradable and that there are 30 unique units because they aren't, and they aren't. But you could probably stretch definitions to claim either ONE for your Steam Storefront.) TLDR: POORLY DESIGNED AND FALSELY ADVERTISED; AS IF THE GAME WAS 80% FINISHED, NEVER PLAY TESTED, AND FORCED TO RELEASE BY A PUBLISHER WHO TACKED AS MANY BUZZWORDS TO THE STEAM STORE PAGE AS POSSIBLE WITHOUT REGARD FOR WHETHER THEY DESCRIBE THE GAME OR NOT. FOR THREE BUCKS ITS A DECENT TIME WASTE AND PLEASANT TO LOOK AT.

[h2]The Good[/h2] [b]Art[/b] My favorite thing is the artstyle! The pixel graphics and animations are excellent, smooth, and charming. Both during gameplay and during the micro-cutscenes between runs. [h2]The Bad[/h2] [b](everything else)[/b] [b]Gameplay / Difficulty[/b] The gameplay has some interesting ideas behind the system, but is far too easy to present any meaningful challenge. After an hour and a half I hadn't taken a single point of damage on my King and never felt any sense of tension. (I was playing on the easiest difficulty but looking at the other reviews, it seems like higher difficulties do not provide interesting challenge). [b]Story[/b] Narrative is barely there and not compelling. (That's fine, it's a roguelite, it doesn't have to. Alas the gameplay does not make up for it.) Disappointing, since the dev could have gone in a direction where you encourage Being Evil or something. This is a necromancy game after all. Instead the 'story' boils down to 'go kill the evil human king that is more evil than you'. Feels like a missed opportunity for something cooler/edgier/unique. [b]Sound[/b] Soundtrack is mediocre. Nothing to write home about, it serves the purpose of filling your ears. Foley / sfx is good. Again, nothing spectacular. [h2]Overall[/h2] [b]Meh.[/b] I probably got $4 worth of entertainment out of this? So it's accurately priced I suppose. I think there's *maybe* potential here, but this needs a lot of tinkering and rebalancing to make the gameplay compelling. This is a shame, I truly do want a game with this premise to be good.

A very easy, repetitive short game. It took me a little over 2 hours to finish the game, in which I never lost a battle or hp. There are very few bosses in the game with unique mechanics, which barely changed my strategy if at all. There are multiple areas you progress through, each one deleting your inventory of cards and deck upgrades, changing it back to default. The only thing kept between areas is your researched cards, which aren't even needed and many are not very useful. There is a "story" but its just text in between swapping areas. The game is infinitely replayabl but it gets boring pretty quickly. If you want a quick, cheap game where you don't have to use much of your brain, you could try this out. (it does not get content updates but does get more point shop items..)

A limited deck-building deckbuilder. I really like the art and concept, but the actual gameplay falls flat and doesn't require much thinking, since mostly you can win by just having decent cards and spamming them. If a really hard fight is coming up, then you slot in more consumables. There's almost nothing in the way of synergies or combos (or if there are, they're hidden after you've already beaten the game several times), so gameplay is almost entirely a matter of saving up mana and cards until the last minute, then spamming as much as possible all at once to make a big wave of skeletons. I'd think about playing more to see if maybe I just need a second full hour of gameplay to get to the good stuff, but when I attacked the wall to the king's castle, the game bugged out and placed an unkillable paladin who just stands there slightly to the right of zone 4, and my army was just walking through the zones over and over until my horse rider leveled up so many times from advancing through zones it crashed the game.

[h2]The Necromancer and the king[/h2] This game was a unique experience to me. The art style reminded me of loop hero -which was one of the primary reasons i bought it. As for the game mechanics and they are pretty simple and straightforward. The map is a vast chessboard-like grid where you come across villages, cities, cemeteries, enemy commanders etc. You build your deck with units and consumables that require mana and/or souls to cast. As you progress your deck becomes stronger -adding more powerful units and better spells. If you are strong enough you beat the final boss -the king- and the next stage awaits. I think there's a lot of potential here but its seems devs gave up on the project. Pity. I bought this dirt-cheap (1.24 Euros) definitely worth your time if turn-based deck-builders are your thing

This is a weird little genre soup, it's part deckbuilder, part tactics game, part autobattler, and somehow all three of those ingredients actually blend together instead of fighting each other for control of the pot. The pitch is simple. The world is rotting, everyone's mad about it, and you, a skeleton wearing a crown, have decided the correct response to societal decay is more decay, but organized and with a deck of skulls.
Scratched a necromancer itch that I've been trying to scratch for a long time.
